For software-related discussions, the operating system is mainly considered when referring to a platform.
Platform dependency means a program expects the platform on which it executes to be the same as the platform for which it was compiled.
If those platforms do not match, execution may not happen.
When a C program is compiled, machine-level instructions are generated for the platform on which compilation happens.
If those compiled instructions are moved to a different platform, they may not execute because the machine-level code is platform dependent.

Because the processor understands machine-level language, not high-level language.
Therefore, the high-level source code must first be converted into machine-level instructions using a compiler.

8. What is the purpose of a linker?
A linker connects the required machine-level code from other files or libraries with the object file.
For example, required functionality from header-related libraries can be linked with the compiled program.
9. What is the purpose of a loader?
A loader brings executable program content from the hard disk into RAM so that it can be executed.
An executable file is the final file produced after the required linking process.
Its contents can be loaded into RAM and then executed by the processor.
